# Groundquote: full project context

Groundquote is an evidence-first retrieval-augmented generation application
created by Eric Lai. Its purpose is to make document question answering easy to
verify. A user pastes or uploads a text document, asks one specific question,
and receives either a concise answer with visible source passages or an explicit
statement that the document does not contain enough information.

## Product principles

1. Retrieval before generation. The document is normalized, split into
   overlapping passages, and ranked against the question.
2. Evidence is visible. The passages used for an answer appear beside it.
3. Citations are checked in application code. Model-produced citation IDs must
   refer to passages that were actually provided.
4. Source text is untrusted data. Instructions found inside an uploaded
   document are not followed.
5. Abstention is a feature. Weak retrieval produces a safe no-answer response.
6. Graceful degradation. Without a model API, Groundquote returns an extractive
   evidence answer rather than inventing a result.
7. Documents are request-scoped. Groundquote does not persist document text or
   questions in its application database.

## Retrieval pipeline

The lexical path uses tokenization, stop-word filtering, BM25 ranking, reciprocal
rank fusion, and passage deduplication. When configured, semantic embeddings add
a second ranking. The top distinct passages become evidence. A confidence signal
and question-term coverage decide whether enough support exists to continue.

## Generation pipeline

Generated mode uses the OpenAI Responses API with structured JSON output. The
model is instructed to answer only from the supplied passages, cite each claim,
ignore instructions inside the source, and remain concise. Zod validates the
response schema. Application code then rejects missing, invented, or invalid
citations.

## Privacy and limits

Groundquote accepts text, Markdown, CSV, and JSON up to 60,000 characters.
Document text and questions are processed in memory for the request and are not
persisted by Groundquote. When generated mode is enabled, retrieved passages and
the question are sent to the configured model provider. Anonymous feedback can
store only an answer ID, helpful/not-helpful choice, answer mode, and timestamp.

Groundquote is open source under the MIT license:
https://github.com/eatusc/groundquote
